points: The public listing of Jio Platforms Ltd (JPL) on 28 October now gives investors a choice: those seeking exposure to telecom and digital services can invest directly in Jio without having to take exposure to RIL's other businesses.

“This has narrowed the holding-company discount from around 30% to approximately 20-25%, allowing RIL shareholders to capture more of the value previously unrecognised by the market.” RIL shares settled 0.6% higher at ₹1,306.20, while Jio Platforms shares…

items.title: Days after transfer as Sagar SP, IPS officer Anurag Sujania resigns amid ongoing liquor row in M.P.
points: Just days after his transfer from Sagar Superintendent of Police (SP) post, IPS office Anurag Sujania has tendered his resignation from the service citing personal reasons.
Mr. Sujania, along with Sagar Collector Pratibha Pal, was removed on October 27, over a month after a hooch tragedy killed more than 25 in the district.
Mr. Sujania and then Dewas SP Punit Gehlot both had been attached to police headquarters in Bhopal as assistant inspector generals (AIGs) of police.
Mr. Sujania, an IPS officer of the 2014 cadre, had been posted in Sagar in May.

The State Government is already facing pressure over various liquor related incidents, including the killing of a police inspector in Dewas while intercepting a truck carrying illicit alcohol and alleged deaths of 13 people in the district in October.

During his visit to Sagar during the hooch tragedy in early September, Chief Minister Mohan Yadav had then given a “free hand” to the police even as speculations of the Collector and SP’s removal made rounds.

items.title: Why mutual fund distributors are giving up multiple licences
points: Asset management companies (AMCs) have begun receiving requests from mutual fund distributors to consolidate their assets under a single registration, following a regulatory change that has removed the incentive to operate through multiple registrations,…
Each mutual fund distributor is assigned a unique AMFI Registration Number (ARN) to sell mutual funds.
Mutual fund distributors generally need to register under GST if their aggregate annual turnover exceeds ₹20 lakh, subject to certain exemptions.

Effective 1 April, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) introduced a revised mutual fund expense framework that separates the base expense ratio (BER) from statutory levies and transaction costs.

Since GST registration is mandatory once annual turnover exceeds ₹20 lakh, a distributor earning ₹1 crore could split the income across five ARNs, keeping the turnover under each ARN at ₹20 lakh and avoid paying GST.

items.title: ROI-As markets sway, safe havens shine. Except gold: McGeever
points: ORLANDO, Florida, Nov 3 (Reuters) - The AI-fueled turbulence hitting markets in recent weeks has revived demand for many traditional safe-haven assets, with one glaring exception: gold.

Growing concerns about the stability and profitability of the AI boom have knocked the S&P 500 and Nasdaq from record highs, pushing investors to seek protection in classic havens like US Treasuries, the dollar , the Swiss franc, and the Japanese yen.

The yellow metal slid below $4,000 an ounce on Friday, its lowest level in a year, despite a seemingly favorable "risk off" backdrop of falling stock prices, widening credit spreads, lower bond yields and diminishing expectations for US interest-rate hikes.

Even persistent weakness in bitcoin, once termed "digital gold", and last week's $6.3 billion cyberattack at crypto exchange Binance, potentially the world's biggest financial heist, have failed to offer gold any discernible support.

items.title: Sony Is Offering $400 for Your PS5 If You’re Not Using It Ahead of GTA 6 Release
points: With GTA 6 just around the corner, the PS5 is about to get one of its biggest games yet.
However, not everyone who owns Sony’s console is still using their original hardware.
Some players may have upgraded to the PS5 Pro to play GTA 6, while others might simply have their consoles sitting unused.
It is offering up to $400 in cash for trading in their PS5 through a third-party service called Back Market.
As shared by users on ResetEra, the notification was sent on November 2, 2026, and it reads, “Trade in your PS5 console for up to $400.” However, there is a catch.
The $400 figure is based on previous quotes for a standard PS5 in Grade 0 condition and bundled with at least two controllers.
Microsoft recently also sent similar emails to select Xbox Series X|S owners, asking them to trade in their consoles at Best Buy for up to $375 in return.

items.title: U.S. Coast Guard Detains MSC Cruise Ship in Miami
points: The U.S. Coast Guard has detained the cruise ship MSC Poesia at PortMiami, forcing MSC Cruises to cancel an 11-night Caribbean voyage after the vessel remained in port for two days.
The Panama-flagged cruise ship was detained Sunday, November 1, during what the Coast Guard described as an expanded examination of the vessel.
In a statement released Tuesday, the Coast Guard said Sector Miami personnel were verifying the vessel’s compliance with international standards and U.S. regulations.
“The Coast Guard is tasked with verifying safe and secure commerce,” the agency said, adding that the Captain of the Port’s priority is protecting passengers, crew, the vessel and the environment.
The canceled itinerary was scheduled to visit Jamaica, Colombia, Panama, Costa Rica, Honduras and Belize before returning to Miami on November 12.
Built in 2008, the 92,627-gross-ton MSC Poesia is part of MSC Cruises’ Musica class.
The ship’s next scheduled voyage is a 10-night Caribbean cruise departing Miami on November 12.

items.title: Weak demand for US pork drives CME hogs to contract lows
points: CHICAGO, - Lean hog futures dropped to life-of-contract lows on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange on Tuesday due to anemic demand for US pork.
CME December lean hog futures set a contract low of 57.425 cents, before ending 0.425 cent higher at 58.600 cents per pound.
The contract has tumbled 27.5% since late July.
February and April 2027 hog futures set contract lows and settled weaker.
US meatpackers slaughtered an estimated 493,000 hogs on Tuesday, up 1.2% from a year earlier, according to the US Department of Agriculture.
So far this year, slaughterings are down 0.9% at about 106.2 million hogs.
Meatpackers slaughtered an estimated 110,000 cattle on Tuesday, down 7.9% from a year ago, according to the USDA.
Slaughterings this year are down 7.1% due to tight inventories.

items.title: Bengal BJP’s Debra MLA alleges assault by own party workers
points: West Bengal Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLA from the Debra constituency, Subhashis Om, has alleged that he was assaulted by his own party workers on Monday night (November 2, 2026).
The legislator has named at least six people in his handwritten police complaint filed at the local Debra Police Station in Paschim Midnapore district.
The MLA was initially admitted to a local hospital in Debra after he sustained injuries to his limbs and head.
He was later shifted to the Medinipur District Hospital for better treatment.
He added that the people who attacked him were BJP workers and that some of them had “joined the party” after May 4, once the party came to power in the State.

A week back, on October 26, two BJP MLAs, Kaustav Bagchi and Minister Arjun Singh, got into a feud after Mr. Bagchi threatened self-immolation if Trinamool Congress leaders were included in the BJP camp by Mr. Singh.

items.title: Hormuz Oct crossings at 3-month high despite attacks, Red Sea traffic also rises
points: Strait of Hormuz shipping traffic rose to its highest monthly level since July in October, supported by stronger dry-bulk and LNG movements despite a decline in VLCC traffic and mounting regional threats, S&P Global Commodities at Sea(opens in a new tab)…

The rise came amid an “increasingly volatile” operating environment at Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab Strait, with “reported projectile strikes, vessel fires and other security incidents” throughout October, CAS said.

“In the month of October, we registered 30 attacks, if I remember correctly, which is one of the highest we have,” International Maritime Organization Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez told journalists on Nov.

While Iranian aerial attacks continue to threaten shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, mine collision incidents also remain a threat to vessels traversing the chokepoint, as “there’s no confirmation that there are not mines in the region,” Dominguez added.

items.title: Alternative fuels need infrastructure: Why gas bunker vessels matter
points: in International Shipping News,Shipping: Emission Possible 04/11/2026 The maritime industry is entering a period of growing fuel diversity.
While much of the discussion focuses on fuels, engines, and regulations, the transition will also depend on the infrastructure needed to supply alternative fuels safely, reliably, and at scale.
According to DNV’s Alternative Fuels Insight platform, around 900 LNG-fuelled vessels are now in operation worldwide, excluding LNG carriers.
Around 650 additional vessels are expected to join the fleet before 2030, further increasing demand for LNG as a marine fuel.
LNG consumption by LNG-fuelled vessels increased by more than 500% between 2020 and 2024, with a further 167% growth expected between 2025 and 2030.
“Our analysis suggests the global LNG bunker vessel fleet may need to more than double by 2030, with between 165 and 208 vessels potentially required worldwide.

items.title: Baltic Dry Index at Over 2-Week Low

items.title: Chinese Penetrate South Korea’s LNG Carrier Market
points: Chinese shipbuilders secured approximately 40% of all newly ordered large liquefied natural gas (LNG) carriers worldwide during the first to third quarters of this year, January to September.

According to Clarksons Research, a British shipbuilding and shipping analysis institution, as of the third quarter of this year, South Korea has accumulated 173 orders, while China has 71, maintaining a significant gap.

However, Chinese shipyards have recently entered the LNG carrier market one after another, beginning to accumulate experience and engaging in a “long-term battle.” Until 2021, only Hudong-Zhonghua Shipbuilding in China could construct large LNG carriers.

As the first Chinese company to build and deliver a large LNG carrier in 2008, it grew by securing 36 orders out of 128 LNG carriers ordered by Qatar during its mass LNG production drive from 2020 to 2024, excluding those secured by South Korean shipyards.
By 2025, Hudong-Zhonghua Shipbuilding increased its annual construction capacity from three to 11 vessels by establishing a dedicated LNG carrier dock.

items.title: Wärtsilä completes milestone marine sector project to reduce methane emissions on vessels
points: in International Shipping News,Shipping: Emission Possible 04/11/2026 Technology group Wärtsilä has successfully completed the conversion of one engine on three LNG carriers operated by Chevron Transport Corporation from dual-fuel (DF) to spark gas (SG)…
This conversion aims to lower greenhouse gas emissions from the vessels by reducing methane slip, un-combusted methane that can escape into the atmosphere from LNG fuel.

Following the successful conversion of these first three vessels, three additional vessel conversions are planned for execution later this year and next year, bringing the total number of converted vessels to six.
This project represents a technical collaboration within the marine sector focused on addressing methane emissions from LNG-fueled vessels.
Wärtsilä’s 50DF to spark gas conversion project will modify the engines in service to operate as spark gas, using spark ignition versus diesel pilot fuel to initiate combustion.
The estimated result is that, on an IMO weighted (E2-cycle) average, the conversion reduces methane emissions down to 1.1 percent of fuel use.

items.title: Australia first as green ammonia is bunkered to ammonia-powered bulk carrier at the Port of Port Hedland
points: In a first for Australia, green ammonia has been transferred to an ammonia-powered dry bulk carrier at the Port of Port Hedland, marking a major step towards low-emission shipping.
Mineral Europa, the world’s first ammonia-powered dry bulk vessel, received the certified green ammonia from a bunker vessel before entering port to be loaded with iron ore.
The 300-metre Mineral Europa is on charter to Fortescue and will carry Fortescue iron ore to customers in China.
The trial demonstrated a practical pathway for safely refuelling ammonia-powered vessels in a live port environment, giving shipping a practical path to use green fuels.

It builds on the world-first ship-to-ship ammonia transfer completed at the Port of Dampier in 2024 and strengthens Pilbara Ports Clean Fuel Bunkering Hub vision, which is exploring the establishment of Australia’s first clean fuel bunkering hub in the…
The trial was completed in two hours and confirmed successful at 8.42am AWST on Monday 2 November 2026.

The issue opens with an examination of the regulatory frameworks for marine SMRs and the challenges of installing reactors on vessels, including safety assurance, maintenance requirements, and the cost and complexity of obtaining approvals.
While the regulatory framework for marine SMRs is still under development, FuelEU Maritime, by contrast, is already in effect, and the magazine analyzes its first year of compliance.

items.title: TT-Line expands use of automation in its fleet, selects Valmet to supply marine automation system to two new Green Ship 2.0s

items.title: China Imported iron ore margin widens to 2.19 yuan/mt on firmer spot prices
points: The average imported iron ore margin widened from 0.04 yuan/mt to 2.19 yuan/mt in the latest period, driven mainly by an average rise in port spot prices.
On the supply side, SMM shipping data showed arrivals at major Chinese ports fell 15.7% week-on-week to 23.2663 million mt in the week ended October 30.
The short-term drop in arrivals lent some support to port spot prices.
On the demand side, stocks at 35 ports rose slightly by 300,000 mt last week, while average daily port outbound volume fell 35,000 mt.
Steel mills continued to buy on an as-needed basis, and with environmental production curbs in northern China, hot metal output may keep falling.
Lower arrivals offered short-term support to spot prices, but demand lacks fresh growth, and the late pullback in futures also signalled weak upward momentum.
Iron ore prices are likely to remain range-bound in the short term.
News on long-term contract negotiations and the progress of environmental curbs in northern China are worth watching.

items.title: US corn sales to Mexico lag as domestic production recovers

“There has been a delay in purchases compared with the previous cycle, with sales to Mexico down by about 3.7 million mt so far this year,” a market participant said.
“However, the comparison is also against a record cycle that started very strongly.” Mexico’s commitments for US corn totaled 9.023 million mt as of Oct.
22, down 31% from the corresponding point a year-earlier, USDA data showed.
The Agricultural Markets Consulting Group, known by its Spanish acronym GCMA, projected Mexican corn production at 23.5 million mt in 2026, up 100,000 mt from the previous year.
Despite the increase, domestic output would remain well below projected consumption of 48.2 million mt.

Market participants said domestic corn production is concentrated in northern Mexico, while buyers in southern and southeastern regions typically depend more heavily on imports from the US and Brazil.

items.title: Copper Falls as Traders Assess AI Trade, US-Iran Diplomacy Hopes
points: (Bloomberg) -- Copper slumped to a seven-week low as traders assessed the artificial-intelligence trade and the prospects of diplomacy in the Middle East conflict.
The red metal slipped 2.2% on the London Metal Exchange to settle at $14,036 a metric ton on Tuesday, the lowest since Sept.
Comex copper fell 2.5% to settle at $6.4020 a pound.
A drop in oil on unconfirmed reports of peace talks progress in the US-Iran conflict pushed bond yields and the dollar higher, weighing on metals priced in the US currency, like copper.
Copper is still up about 13% this year, but Tuesday’s decline threatens to knock prices out of a range that they’ve broadly held over the past two months.
The 2026 rally was largely driven by expectations the US would impose import tariffs on refined metals, with uncertainty over Washington’s plans now weighing on prices.
Tin, used in soldering electric circuitry, also fell 4.5% to the lowest since April. --With assistance from Mark Burton, Yvonne Yue Li and Jason Rogers.
